blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: XP — Agile method emphasising disciplined engineering practices.
TDD — Write a failing test then implement/refactor.
RAD — Development centred on rapid prototyping and user feedback.
refactoring — Improving structure without changing observable behaviour.

blocks.title: XP practices
blocks.text: Test-driven development, pair programming, refactoring and continuous integration.

blocks.title: RAD approach
blocks.text: Rapid application development uses prototyping and stakeholder collaboration.

blocks.title: Balance cost and fit
blocks.text: Consider user availability, architecture, maintainability and regulatory oversight.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: Automated tests written before/with code (TDD) define intended behaviour, continuous integration runs regression tests on each change, and refactoring improves design without changing observable behaviour. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.

blocks.title: Shared worked answer
blocks.text: Create an early working prototype, invite feedback, revise the interface rapidly and iteratively converge on requirements. Beware treating a rushed prototype as production-quality architecture without further work.
